questions.q: Why not just delete the unanswered call?
questions.a: Dropping the whole unfinished turn gives a valid history, but the model forgets it may already have acted, and might act again. Keeping the call with an error result tells it the truth.

questions.q: What if the model called three tools and the crash came after two finished?
questions.a: All three results must go back together. Save the turn only once every result is in, or fill the missing one with an error result.

teach.title: How it works: closing the gap

questions.q: State the rule the crash broke, in one sentence.
questions.a: Every tool call must be followed, in the very next message, by a result with the same id.

questions.q: Why does every message look fine while the API rejects the history?
questions.a: The problem isn't in any one message. It's a missing partner: a call whose result was never saved.

questions.q: Name the two halves of the fix.
questions.a: Save each turn (call plus results) as one all-or-nothing unit, and make tools safe to repeat with an idempotency key. Then check the history on resume and repair any gap.
